source_text: Sr autem quidam tentaverint allegorisare hee que ejusmodi sunt, neque de omnibus poterunt consonantes sibimetipsis inveniri, et convincentur ab ipsis dictionibus disserentibus, quoniam cum desolate fuerint civitates gentium, e¢ quod non inhabitentur, et domus, eo quod non sint homines, et derelinquetur terra deserta; Ecce enim, Esaias ait, dies Domini insanabilis venit, furore et ira plenus, ponere urbem terre desertam, et peccatores perdere ex ea. Et iterum ait: Tollatur, ut non videat gloriam Domini, et cum hee facta fuerint, elongabit, inquit, Deus homines, et derelicti multiplicabuntur in terra. Et wdificabunt domus, et ipsi inhabitabunt, et pastinabunt vineas, et ipsi manducabunt. in resurrectionem justorum sine controversia dicta sunt, que fit post adventum Antichristi, et perditionem omnium gentium sub— exsistentium, in qua regnabunt justi in terra, crescentes- ex visione Domini, et per ipsum assuescent capere gloriam Dei unitatem spiritalium in regno capient: et illos quos in carne inveniet, exspectantes eum de ccelis, et perpessos tribu-— lationem, qui et effugerint iniqui manus. Ipsi autem sunt de quibus ait propheta: e¢ derelicti multiplicabuntur in terra. Et quotquot ex credentibus ad hoe preeparavit Deus, ad derelictos — in terra, et sub Regno Sanctorum fieri, et minis-— trare huic Hierusalem, et regnum in ea, significavit 1Jeremias propheta: Circumspice, dicens, ad Orientem Hierusalem, et Letitiam que adventat tibi ab ipso Deo. Ecce venient filit tui quos emisisti, venient collecti ab Oriente usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ea que a Deo tuo est claritate. Exuere Hierusalem habitum luctus et afflictionis tue, et induere decorem ejus que a Deo tuo est claritatis in awternum: circumdare amictum duplicem ejus que a Deo tuo est justitie, impone mitram super caput tuum glorie eterne. Deus enim demonstrabit ei quae sub colo est universe tuum fulgorem. Vocabitur namque nomen tuum ab ipso Deo in weternum, pax justitice et glorie colenti Deo. Surge Hierusalem, et sta in excelso, et circumspice ad Orientem, et vide collectos filios tuos a Solis ortu usque ad Occidentem verbo illius sancti, gaudentes ipsam Dei recordationem. Profecti sunt enim a@ pedites, dum adducerentur ab inimicis. Introducet illos Deus ad te portatus cum gloria tanquam thronus regni. Decrevit enim Deus ut humilietur omnis mons excelsus, et congeries eterne, et ut valles impleantur, ad redigendam planitiem terre, ut ambulet Israel tute Dei gloria. Umbracula autem intewuerunt syloc, et lignum boni odoris ipsi Israel pracepto Dei. Provibit enim Deus cum letitia lumine claritatis suc, cum misericordia et justitia, quae ab ipso est. 2. Heec autem talia universa non in superccelestibus possunt intelligi: Deus enim, ait, demonstrabit ei que sub caclo est, universe tuum fulgorem; sed in Regni temporibus, revocata terra a Christo, et reedificata Hierusalem, secundum characterem qui ssursum est Hierusalem, de qua ait propheta Esaias: Zece in manibus meis depinai muros tuos, et in conspectu meo es semper. Et Apostolus autem scribens ad Galatas similiter ait: J//a autem que surswm est Hierusalem libera est, que est mater omnium nostrum ; non ex cogitatione erratici AXonis dicens hoc, neque virtute aliqua, que abscessit Pleromate, et Prunico; sed de Hierusalem quee in manibus descripta est. Et ipsam descendentem in Apocalypsi vidit Johannes super terram, novam. Post enim Regni tempora, Vidi, inquit, thronum album magnum, et sedentem in eo, cujus a facie fugit terra et colum, et locus non est eis. Et illa jam quee sunt generalis resurrectionis et judicii exponit vidisse, dicens mortuos magnos et minores. Dedit, inquit, > mare mortuos quos in se habuit, et mors et infert dederunt mortuos quos apud se habuerunt: et libri adaperti sunt. Sed et vite, ait, ,, apertus est liber, et judicati sunt mortui ex vis que scripta erant in libris, secundum opera sua: et mors et inferi missi sunt in stagnum ignis, secundam mortem. Hoe autem est quod vocatur Gehenna, quod Dominus dixit ignem zternum. Zt si quis, inquit, non est inventus in libro vite scriptus, missus est in stagnum ignis. Et post heee ait: Vidi calum nowwm et terram novam: Primum enim calum et terra abierunt, etiam mare non est. Et civitatem sanctam Hierusalem novam vidi descendentem de colo, preparatam ut sponsam ornatam viro suo. Et audivi, inquit, vocem magnam de throno dicentem: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis, et ipsi populi ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit corum Deus. Et delebit omnem lacrymam ab oculis eorum, et mors non erit amplius, non luctus non clamor neque dolor ulterius erit, quia prima abierunt. Et Esaias autem hoe ipsum ait: Erit enim obveniet eis in cor; sed latitiam et exultationem invenient in ea. autem est quod ab Apostolo dictum est: Preterit enim habitus hujus mundi. Similiter autem et Dominus ait: Terra et celum transiet. ~His itaque preetereuntibus super terram, novam superiorem Hierusalem ait Domini discipulus Johannes dere, quemadmodum sponsam ornatam viro suo; et hoe esse tabernaculum Dei, in quo inhabitabit Deus cum hominibus, HujusHierusalem imago illa, que in priori terra Hierusalem, in qua Sjusti preemeditantur incorruptelam, et parantur in salutem, Et hujus tabernaculi typum accepit Moyses in monte: et nihil allegorisari potest, sed omnia firma et vera, et substantiam habentia, ad fruitionem hominum justorum a Deo facta. Quomodo enim vere Deus est, qui resuscitat hominem; sic et vere resurgit a mortuis, et non allegorice, quemadmodum per tanta ostendimus.* Et sicut vere resurgit, sic et vere praemeditabitur ineorruptelam, et augebitur, et vigebit in regni temporibus, ut fiat CapaX glorize Patris. Deinde omnibus renovatis, vere in civitate habitabit Dei. Diwit, enim inquit, sedens super thronum: Ecce nova facio omnia. Et dicit Dominus; Omnia scribe, quomodo tt sermones fideles, et veri sunt. Et divit mihi, Facta sunt. Et secundum rationem.
thought_title: The Resurrection and the New Jerusalem
pass_a_gloss: But if certain ones have attempted to allegorize these things which are of this kind, they will not be able to be found consonant with themselves in all things, and they will be convinced by the very words which they discuss, for when the cities of the nations have been deserted, because they are not inhabited, and the houses, because there are no men, and the earth has been left deserted; For behold, Isaiah says, the day of the Lord is coming, incurable and full of fury and anger, to put the city on the earth deserted, and to destroy sinners from it. And again he says: Let him be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord, and when these things have been done, God will prolong, he says, the days of men, and the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth. And they will build houses, and they themselves will inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards, and they themselves will eat. These things have been spoken without controversy concerning the resurrection of the just, which occurs after the coming of the Antichrist, and the destruction of all the nations which exist under heaven, in which the just will reign on the earth, growing from the vision of the Lord, and through him they will become accustomed to taking the glory of God, the unity of spiritual things in the kingdom. And those whom he finds in the flesh, waiting for him from heaven, and having endured tribulation, who have also escaped the hands of the wicked. These are the ones about whom the prophet says: and the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth. And as many as God has prepared from the believers for this, to be deserted on the earth, and to be under the Kingdom of the Saints, and to minister to this Jerusalem, and the kingdom in it, the prophet Jeremiah has signified, saying: Look around, he says, to the East, Jerusalem, and the joy which comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you have sent out will come, they will come gathered from the East to the West by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the things which are from your God, with clarity. Put off, Jerusalem, the garment of mourning and your affliction, and put on the adornment of that which is from your God, with clarity, forever. Surround yourself with a double garment of the justice which is from your God, put a mitre on your head, of eternal glory. For God will show to her what is under the whole heaven, your splendor. For your name will be called by God himself, forever, peace, justice, and glory, worshiping God. Arise, Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look around to the East, and see your sons gathered from the rising of the sun to the West, by the word of that holy one, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they have gone forth on foot, while they were being led by their enemies. God will introduce them to you, carried with glory, like a throne of the kingdom. For God has decreed that every high mountain will be humbled, and the eternal gatherings, and that the valleys will be filled, to reduce the plain of the earth, so that Israel may walk securely in the glory of God. And the tabernacles have overshadowed the sycamores, and the tree of good odor, by the command of God, for Israel. For God will prohibit with joy, the light of his clarity, with mercy and justice, which are from him. But these things, of this kind, cannot be understood in the supercelestial things: for God, he says, will show to her what is under the whole heaven, your splendor; but in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been recalled by Christ, and Jerusalem has been rebuilt, according to the character which is above, Jerusalem, about which the prophet Isaiah says: I have depicted your walls in my hands, and you are always in my sight. And the Apostle, writing to the Galatians, says similarly: But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all; not from the thought of the erratic Aeons, saying this, nor by any virtue which has departed from the Pleroma, and the Prunicus; but from the Jerusalem which has been described in the hands. And he saw this Jerusalem descending upon the earth, new, in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, I saw, he says, a great white throne, and one sitting on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled, and there was no place for them. And he explains the things which are of the general resurrection and judgment, saying, I saw the dead, great and small. The sea, he says, gave up the dead which it had, and death and hell gave up the dead which they had; and the books were opened. And the book of life, he says, was opened, and the dead were judged from the things which were written in the books, according to their works; and death and hell were cast into the lake of fire, into the second death. This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord said is eternal fire. And if anyone, he says, has not been found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire. And after these things, he says, I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and there is no longer any sea. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, descending from heaven, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard, he says, a great voice from the throne, saying: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them, their God. And he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death, no more mourning, no more crying, no more pain, for the former things have passed away. And Isaiah says the same thing: for it will be a joy and an exultation which they will find in it. But this is what has been said by the Apostle: for the fashion of this world has passed away. Similarly, the Lord says: the earth and the heaven will pass away. When these things have passed away, the Lord's disciple, John, says that there will be a new Jerusalem above, like a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. The image of this Jerusalem is that which is in the former earth, Jerusalem, in which the just are prepared for incorruption, and are prepared for salvation. And Moses received the type of this tabernacle on the mountain: and nothing can be allegorized, but all things are firm and true, and have substance, made by God for the enjoyment of just men. For just as God is truly, who raises man; so also truly does he rise from the dead, and not allegorically, as we have shown through so many things. And just as he truly rises, so also will he truly prepare incorruption, and will increase, and will flourish in the times of the kingdom, so that he may become the glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For he says, sitting on the throne: Behold, I make all things new. And the Lord says: Write all things, how my words are faithful and true. And he says to me: They have been made. And according to reason.

pass_b_english: If some have tried to allegorize these matters, they will not be found consistent with themselves in every respect, and the very words they discuss will convict them. For when the cities of the nations have been deserted, because they are not inhabited, and the houses, because there are no men, and the earth has been left desolate — behold, Isaiah says: the day of the Lord is coming, incurable, full of fury and anger, to make the land a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it (Isaiah 13:9). And again he says: Let him be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord (Isaiah 13:19); and when these things have come to pass, God will remove men far away, and the forsaken will multiply on the earth. And they will build houses and inhabit them; they will plant vineyards and eat the fruit. These things are spoken without controversy concerning the resurrection of the just, which takes place after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all nations under heaven, in which the just will reign on the earth, growing through the vision of the Lord, and through him becoming accustomed to receive the glory of God, the unity of spiritual things, in the kingdom. And those whom he finds in the flesh, waiting for him from heaven and having endured tribulation, who have also escaped the hands of the wicked — these are the ones of whom the prophet says: the forsaken will multiply on the earth. And as many as God has prepared from among believers for this purpose, to be left on the earth and to be under the Kingdom of the Saints, and to minister to this Jerusalem, and the kingdom within it, the prophet Jeremiah has signified, saying: Look toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you sent away shall come; they shall come gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory that comes from your God (Jeremiah 31:8–9). Put off, Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on the beauty of the glory from your God forever. Wrap yourself in the double mantle of righteousness from your God; set upon your head the mitre of eternal glory. For God will show your splendor to every eye under heaven. Your name shall be named by God forever: Peace of Righteousness and Glory of God's Worship. Arise, Jerusalem, stand on the height; look toward the east and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they went out on foot, led away by enemies; but God will bring them back to you, borne in glory as on a royal throne. For God has decreed that every high mountain shall be humbled and the everlasting hills, and the valleys filled up, to make the ground level, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God. The woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel at God's command. For God will lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory, with mercy and righteousness that proceed from him (Baruch 5:1–9).

Now such things as these cannot be understood as belonging to a super-celestial realm; for God, he says, will show her your splendor under the whole heaven — but in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been reclaimed by Christ and Jerusalem rebuilt according to the pattern of the Jerusalem which is above, of which the prophet Isaiah says: I have engraved your walls upon my palms; you are ever before me (Isaiah 49:16). And the Apostle, writing to the Galatians, says the same: But the Jerusalem above is free; she is our mother (Galatians 4:26) — not speaking from the fantasy of errant Aeons, nor from any virtue that fell from the Pleroma, nor from Prunicus, but from the Jerusalem depicted in God's hands. And John saw this Jerusalem descending upon the earth, new, in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, he says: I saw a great white throne, and him who sat upon it; from his face earth and heaven fled away, and no place was found for them (Revelation 20:11). And he describes the general resurrection and judgment: I saw the dead, great and small. The sea gave up the dead in it; Death and Hades gave up the dead in them; and books were opened. Also the book of life was opened, and the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to their works. And Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire — this is the second death, the Gehenna of which the Lord spoke, eternal fire. And if anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:12–15). And after this he says: I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (Revelation 21:1–2). And I heard a loud voice from the throne: Behold, the dwelling of God is with men; he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes; death shall be no more, neither mourning nor crying nor pain any more, for the former things have passed away (Revelation 21:3–4). And Isaiah says the same: they shall find joy and exultation in it (Isaiah 65:18). This is what the Apostle said: The form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:31). Likewise the Lord says: Heaven and earth will pass away (Matthew 24:35). When these things have passed away, the Lord's disciple John says there will be a new Jerusalem above, like a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. The image of this Jerusalem is that Jerusalem on the former earth, in which the just are prepared for incorruption and made ready for salvation. And Moses received the pattern of this tabernacle on the mountain. Nothing here can be allegorized; all is firm, true, and substantial, made by God for the enjoyment of the just. For just as God truly raises man, so he truly rises from the dead — not allegorically, as we have shown at length. And just as he truly rises, so he will truly put on incorruption, and increase, and flourish in the times of the kingdom, that he may become the glory of the Father. Then, when all things are renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For he who sits upon the throne says: Behold, I make all things new (Revelation 21:5). And the Lord says: Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true. And he said to me: It is done. And this is according to reason.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful rendering of the clauses, and Pass B provides a polished version that includes appropriate scripture citations (e.g., Isaiah 13:9, Revelation 20:11, etc.) which are required for patristic texts containing biblical quotations. The translation of 'Gehenna' and the description of the resurrection and the New Jerusalem match the source. All arguments and nuances regarding the rejection of allegorization are preserved.
